stories.title: The efficiency trap: why optimising everything can backfire, badly
summary: A protective flu jab offers some reassurance, but so does the thought that there will be a hospital bed for you, should you need it.

Yet, in England, about 95% of adult hospital beds were occupied at the height of flu season last year.If hospitals were hotels, that level of occupancy would be good business, and we would commend them for their efficiency.
But do we really want a hospital to have so few beds in reserve that it’s just one bad flu week away from having to treat patients in corridors?

stories.title: FAA announces first US digital air traffic control towers in Florida and Alaska
summary: Systems provide 360-degree view of airport operations, but concerns have been raised about the technologyThe Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that the first digital air traffic control towers in the US are officially operational, bringing new technology first to smaller airports in Florida and Alaska as the Trump administration presses ahead with updating the country’s ageing aviation infrastructure.The systems are now online at the Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and the Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska, with five additional regional airports slated to receive the technology next.
